sources.title: West and Central Africa Region Humanitarian Situation Report No. 1: 1 January to 30 June 2025
sources.temporal_coverage: Regional report dated 29 August 2025; São Tomé and Príncipe section covers recurring risks and events in December 2021, May 2024 and 2025.
sources.methodology: UNICEF operational situation report summarizing country needs, hazards and agency responses for January-June 2025.
sources.limitations: Self-reported operational synthesis; some country hazard details refer to 2021 and 2024 events.

sources.title: Rising Waters, Rising Hopes: Shaping Resilience in São Tomé and Príncipe Through Flood Risk Analysis
sources.organization: World Bank; authors include a Natural Resources Management Specialist and report contributors
sources.temporal_coverage: Summary of World Bank national flood-risk assessment using present-climate data and projections for 2050 and 2080; published 2 May 2024.
sources.methodology: Report-author summary of high-resolution riverine and coastal flood-risk modelling under SSP3-7.0, without additional climate policy.
sources.limitations: Accessible blog summary, not the full technical report; selected household interviews are illustrative, not representative.

sources.title: São Tomé’s Água Grande District advances local disaster resilience
sources.organization: United Nations Office for Disaster Risk Reduction, Regional Office for Africa
sources.temporal_coverage: District resilience assessment conducted 7-9 September 2026; article dated 6 October 2026.
sources.methodology: UNDRR account of a district scorecard workshop involving public agencies, civil society and sector representatives.
sources.limitations: The account describes an assessment and draft strategy inputs, not an adopted plan or measured resilience outcomes.

sources.title: Enhance Adaptive Capacity to Floods and Water Security in São Tomé and Principe
sources.organization: United Nations Development Programme, Climate Change Adaptation platform; Global Environment Facility project information
sources.temporal_coverage: Project concept/PIF approval shown as June 2024; webpage presents proposed outcomes and beneficiary estimates, not completed results.
sources.methodology: UNDP project-platform summary of the project concept, target population, design and expected outputs.
sources.limitations: The page labels the funding source as pipeline; stated outcomes and beneficiary reach are planned, not evaluated achievements.

claims.locator: Country subsection ‘Situation Overview & Humanitarian Needs’, PDF p. 14, paragraphs 1-2.
claims.paraphrase: UNICEF identifies rainy-season flood, landslide, erosion and drought exposure in mountainous and riverside areas, naming Ribeira Afonso, Malanza and Neves as disproportionately affected.
claims.limitations: Regional situation report; no district-level comparative risk estimates are provided.

claims.locator: Country subsection ‘Situation Overview & Humanitarian Needs’, PDF p. 14, paragraphs 2-3.
claims.paraphrase: After December 2021 floods, Lembá District recorded 2,104 people affected and two child deaths; damage included bridges, a water plant, crops, fishing boats and over half of latrines.
institutions: Government of São Tomé and Príncipe
claims.limitations: Event-specific figures describe December 2021 impacts, not current exposure levels.

claims.locator: Country subsection ‘Situation Overview & Humanitarian Needs’, PDF p. 14, paragraph 4.
claims.paraphrase: After May 2024 floods damaged Príncipe infrastructure and livelihoods, UNICEF reports launching support for over 7,400 families within 72 hours and mobilizing an estimated US$475,000.
claims.limitations: UNICEF reports planned support and mobilization; independent outcome evaluation is not given.

claims.locator: Country subsection ‘Nutrition’, PDF p. 14, first paragraph.
claims.paraphrase: UNICEF says irregular rainfall and prolonged dry spells threaten fragile food systems, particularly for vulnerable households, while food insecurity persisted.
claims.limitations: The report does not disaggregate these food-system effects by district.

claims.paraphrase: The World Bank authors summarize modeled annual flood losses rising from 1.9% of GDP in 2020 to 2.8% in 2050 and 4.1% in 2080 under SSP3-7.0 without additional climate policy.
claims.scenario: SSP3-7.0, assuming no additional climate policy.
claims.limitations: Modelled annual expected losses use 2020 exposure and do not include additional exposure growth.

claims.paraphrase: The assessment identifies Malanza and Santa Catarina among the most affected subdistricts; about 18,500 people are flood-affected annually on average under present-climate conditions.
claims.limitations: A technical-report search excerpt and the accessible summary give reversed district percentages; percentages are therefore omitted.

claims.locator: Article paragraphs beginning ‘Disasters like this feed news stories’ and interview summaries.
claims.paraphrase: World Bank feature interviews portray recurrent flood and wave damage as a livelihood concern for a fisherwoman in Praia Cruz and a fish trader in Praia Abade.
claims.limitations: These selected interviews illustrate experiences; they are not representative prevalence estimates.

claims.locator: Article paragraphs beginning ‘How exposed to disasters’ and ‘From risk assessment to a shared picture of resilience’.
claims.paraphrase: Água Grande District convened more than 20 cross-sector representatives in September 2026 to assess urban risk, including gender and disability organizations, civil protection and meteorological services.
claims.limitations: Participation and assessment activity are documented; no outcomes from later implementation are reported.

claims.locator: Article subsection ‘From risk assessment to a shared picture of resilience’, paragraphs 1-3; ‘Building blocks for a strategy’, paragraphs 1-2.
claims.paraphrase: Participants used the city resilience scorecard to agree priority gaps and draft objectives and coordination arrangements; UNDRR says a full district strategy and action plan remain future work.
claims.limitations: The scorecard and strategy elements are draft planning inputs, not adopted plans or measured outcomes.

claims.locator: Article subsection ‘Risk becomes everyone’s business’, paragraph 2.
claims.paraphrase: Água Grande’s tourism director said flooding and coastal erosion expose tourism, while the existing tourism development plan does not address disaster risk.
claims.limitations: This is a district official’s reported assessment of a plan; it is not an independent plan review.

claims.locator: Project Summary and Detailed Description, paragraphs on São Tomé and Santo António water security.
claims.paraphrase: UNDP’s project page describes climate-driven urban flooding and water-system turbidity affecting São Tomé and Santo António, with interruptions for about one-third of the population and added water-collection burdens for women and girls.
institutions: Government of São Tomé and Príncipe
claims.limitations: Project-page diagnosis is not a new population survey; it provides no city-level breakdown of affected people.

claims.locator: Detailed Description, paragraphs on proposed outcomes and outputs 1.1-4.2.
claims.paraphrase: The proposed package includes climate-resilient water, waste and drainage coordination, watershed management in Água Grande, priority drainage works, and water-quality monitoring in the Água Grande and Santo António basins.
institutions: Directorate of Environment and Climate Action
Government of São Tomé and Príncipe
claims.limitations: These are proposed project activities; the page gives no evidence of implementation or effectiveness.

access_audit.locator: IMF Selected Issues chapter on São Tomé and Príncipe’s resilience to natural disasters.
access_audit.notes: Direct opening returned 403. No claims rely on this page or on search snippets.

search_audit.query: São Tomé and Príncipe climate flood vulnerability district Malanza Santa Catarina official report 2024 World Bank
search_audit.outcome: Found UNICEF event detail for Lembá and named northern/southern communities, and a World Bank district-risk analysis summarized by its authors; exact district percentages differed between indexed PDF text and blog summary and were omitted.

search_audit.query: São Tomé and Príncipe climate change conflict social cohesion political instability resource competition explicit link report
search_audit.outcome: The targeted search did not identify an inspected country-specific primary source explicitly linking climate hazards to conflict, violence or a named FCV mediator; no link is inferred from co-occurring hazard and social vulnerability.

search_audit.query: São Tomé and Príncipe floods landslides insecurity conflict humanitarian access adaptation project delayed violence report
search_audit.outcome: No inspected source established conflict or insecurity disrupting a named climate-adaptation or disaster-response activity. UNICEF describes rapid flood response; UNDRR describes local risk planning, with no violence constraint reported.

search_audit.query: São Tomé and Príncipe community resilience adaptation project evaluation water security women flood resilience named communities report 2025 2026
search_audit.outcome: Found a 2026 Água Grande cross-sector scorecard and draft-planning process plus a UNDP project concept for water coordination and drainage; neither establishes completed adaptation outcomes.

gaps: No inspected primary source established a country-specific climate-to-conflict or violence pathway, or an FCV constraint on adaptation delivery; this remains a documented search gap.

The World Bank technical flood-risk PDF exceeded the web reader's 10 MB content limit. Its accessible author summary supports claims, but the report-index excerpt and summary disagreed on district percentages; percentages are omitted pending direct report review.
The 2026 Country Climate and Development Report is disclosed in Portuguese and was not fully reviewed in this extraction; no claims rely on it.
The accessible UNDP page presents project design and beneficiary estimates, and labels funding pipeline; it does not verify implementation, reach or outcomes.
UNDRR reports draft local strategy inputs for Água Grande, not an adopted district plan or completed resilience outcomes.
The UNICEF report is an operational situation report; its specific event statistics describe 2021 and 2024 shocks rather than current district risk prevalence.
